original_question: Assume the Riemann Hypothesis and a smoothed quaternary additive divisor conjecture. Starting from the conjectured asymptotic I4(T) ~ C4 T (log T)^16 for the eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function, derive the full main term up to an error of size o(T) or a power saving, obtain a shifted analogue, and asymptotically evaluate the smoothed shifted integral of product_{j=1}^4 zeta(1/2 + a_j + it) zeta(1/2 + b_j - it) when |a_j| and |b_j| are << 1/log T and omega is supported in [c1 T, c2 T].
target_in_paper: Problems — Moments of the Riemann zeta function — Problem (8).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem very closely: it has the right conditional hypotheses (the Riemann Hypothesis plus a smoothed quaternary additive divisor conjecture), the right starting asymptotic I_4(T) ~ C_4 T (log T)^16, the demand to upgrade this to the full main term with an o(T) or power-saving remainder, the request for a shifted analogue, and the specific smoothed shifted integral with four pairs of small complex shifts and a weight supported on [c_1 T, c_2 T].
missing_details: The paper’s notation defines I_k(T)=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^(2k) dt, so I_4(T) is the eighth moment; this should be stated explicitly to make the question stand-alone.
The asymptotic regime T→∞ (equivalently, for all sufficiently large T) is implicit in your draft and should be made explicit.
In the paper, the phrase full main term is best read together with Problem (4): for k=4 it means recovering the entire polynomial main term T P_16(log T), not merely the leading constant C_4.
The shifts should be quantified as complex numbers a_j,b_j for j=1,...,4, with the uniform size condition |a_j|,|b_j| << 1/log T.
The weight should be specified as a smooth compactly supported function ω on the real line whose support is contained in [c_1 T, c_2 T], with positive real constants 0<c_1<c_2.

The paper names the smoothed quaternary additive divisor conjecture but does not restate its precise formulation in Problem (8), so a fully stand-alone version should either keep it exactly as a named hypothesis or explicitly say it is the same conjectural input used there.

Problem (8) separately asks for a shifted analogue of the eighth-moment asymptotic and for an asymptotic evaluation of the displayed smoothed shifted integral; those two targets should remain distinct in the rewritten question.
refined_question: Let I_4(T):=∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^8 dt, the eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function. Assume the Riemann Hypothesis and the smoothed quaternary additive divisor conjecture. Starting from the conditional asymptotic I_4(T)∼C_4 T(log T)^16 for some positive constant C_4, prove as T→∞ a full asymptotic formula of the shape I_4(T)=T P_16(log T)+o(T) (or with a power-saving error term), where P_16 is the degree-16 polynomial giving the complete main term; obtain a corresponding shifted analogue; and, under the same hypotheses, asymptotically evaluate ∫_{-∞}^{∞} ω(t)∏_{j=1}^4 ζ(1/2+a_j+it)ζ(1/2+b_j-it) dt for complex shifts a_j,b_j (j=1,...,4) satisfying |a_j|,|b_j|<<1/log T, where ω is a smooth compactly supported function with support contained in [c_1 T,c_2 T] for positive constants 0<c_1<c_2.
justification: This is the exact target because your draft matches Problem (8) in the paper almost verbatim. To make it fully stand-alone while staying narrow, I added the paper’s definition of I_k(T) from the Notation section, made the T→∞ quantifier explicit, and used the nearby general moment formulation in Problem (4) to sharpen full main term into the complete polynomial main term T P_16(log T) for k=4. I did not replace the named conjectural hypothesis by a broader or different one, because Problem (8) itself states it only by name. The relevant places are Introduction, eq. (6), p. 2; Notation, p. 5; Problems (4), p. 6; and Problems (8), p. 7.
